status_summary: DOJ's Office of Legal Counsel concluded on 2025-07-11 that the Hyde Amendment bars HHS funding of transportation to obtain an abortion outside its exceptions, noting that the question arises most often for children in ORR care. In October 2025 a conservative outlet reported that HHS was reviewing the 2024 Unaccompanied Children Program Foundational Rule, and in January 2026 the same outlet reported that ORR had submitted changes on abortion funding for unaccompanied children for OMB review. A women's rights magazine reported on 2026-04-04 that the planned rule, described as updates to accord with the Hyde Amendment, had been announced but its text had not been released. Federal Register searches found no proposed rule as of 2026-10-13.

timeline.event: DOJ Office of Legal Counsel withdraws its 2022 Hyde opinion and concludes Hyde bars HHS funding of abortion-related transportation outside the exceptions; it notes the issue arises most often for children in ORR care.
Outlet reports HHS is reviewing the 2024 Unaccompanied Children Program Foundational Rule and related guidance for Hyde compliance.
Outlet reports ORR has submitted regulatory changes on abortion funding for unaccompanied minors to OMB review.
Magazine reports the announced ORR rule to accord with the Hyde Amendment had not yet been released in text.

title: Stop ORR from facilitating abortions for unaccompanied children in its custody
uncertainties: No ORR policy withdrawal, instruction to care providers or proposed rule was found; a Federal Register search of documents mentioning the Unaccompanied Children Program since 2025-01-20 and of Hyde Amendment documents since July 2025 returned no abortion-related ORR rule, and the HHS regulatory agenda published 2026-08-14 lists no such entry. The OMB submission is reported by a single outlet citing an unnamed official. Reports that ORR routed pregnant children to a Texas shelter from July 2025 were seen only in an aggregator and were not used. The proposal to move ORR to DHS is tracked in another record.
